title: Officers lacked background info
article: A routine query of Jacqueline Montgrand's history with Prince Albert city police revealed she had a propensity for violence and was an escape risk.

But officers attending a call after she refused to be evicted from a home did not have time to receive that information, as shots were fired four seconds after the query was made, a coroner's inquest into Montgrand's death heard Thursday.
Montgrand died after being shot March 18, 2008, by an officer who testified he thought he was in danger after the woman came at him with a knife.

Insp. Brian Bonkowski, who was asked to testify after the jury presented some questions, told jurors it was at the officer's discretion to ask about records and inquiries were not common at "eviction calls."
Lawyer Mitchell Holash, who is representing the Prince Albert Police Service, said the information didn't come into evidence before because it was not seen as relevant.
According to Holash, the general query would provide officers information for grounds for arrest, but Bonkowski said a better practice at eviction calls is for no arrest to occur.
In this case, Montgrand had no warrants.
